chapter: Performing and the idea of free jazz
title: Practising, memory work and Jackie McLean's book
summary: Discussing playing Nonaah, he describes working on memorization and recommends Jackie McLean's exercise book.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: When I heard it I imagined it in an etude book and getting to that page and saying oh there’s no way I’m going to be able to play this.
I am a saxophone player yes.
Oh. You can play it but you’ve just got to stay with it.

Because like man I’m here working like a dog right now man, you know, I mean trying to figure out all different kinds of ways to memorize things more quickly and so on, and then sometimes I get so wrapped up in the stuff and I forget the stuff that I’m working on you know so then I’ll be playing — “Oh I used to play that, I used to play this, I used to do this, I used to do that.” So and then I’m pulling all that back out you know, so that I’m doing that. Because I’m working on memory you know and trying to — so, and it’s working. I’ll tell you a good book is Jackie McLean’s book you know. Do you know that book?

Yeah, that’s a good book man, he takes you to all those choruses and so on and then at the end you have the grand exercises and so on and so on and so forth you know. I mean Jackie Mac is a mean individual. You know. I mean [scats] you know, the thing on
“Stella By Starlight” you know so yeah man, you know there’s no lack of things to do. No lack of things to do.
